name: MoD (Mixture of Demonstrations)
venue: NeurIPS 2024 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37)
authors_affiliation: Song Wang (equal), Zihan Chen (equal), Chengshuai Shi, Cong Shen, Jundong Li -- all University of Virginia.
task_domain: NLP in-context learning: text classification (sentiment, paraphrase, NLI, commonsense reasoning) and generation (open-domain QA, code generation, semantic parsing). Not an agent/planning task; this is ICL demonstration retrieval.
problem_setting: Offline, non-interactive, single-LLM in-context learning. Given a labeled demonstration pool D = {(x_i, y_i)} and a test query x_test, select a set S(x_test) of L demonstrations (default L set to 50, truncated to fit context) to condition a frozen pretrained LLM for few-shot prediction. Supervision is available via the LLM's output log-probability used as a per-demonstration utility signal; retriever models are trained offline and frozen at test time. Single-agent, no environment interaction.
what_is_retrieved: In-context demonstrations (labeled input-output example pairs) drawn from a training-set demonstration pool.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed labeled training-set demonstration pool partitioned offline into expert clusters; no growing/episodic memory written at test time.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Set-level completeness rather than independent top-k: experts collaboratively assemble a complete L-sized demonstration SET, with per-expert quotas |S_i| = floor(h(C_i, x_test) * L). Expert-wise training explicitly optimizes each candidate to be the most helpful demonstration GIVEN the other L-1 already-selected demonstrations are optimal, modeling set-level interaction. Emphasized for compositional datasets requiring precise retrieval of multiple all-important, mutually-dissimilar demonstrations.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not framed as case-based reasoning; only a Retrieve-analogue exists, no Reuse/Revise/Retain cycle).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False -- the work is framed as demonstration retrieval for ICL via a mixture-of-experts paradigm; it does not cite or position itself as case-based reasoning (no Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner grounding).
retrieval_unit: Single demonstration (one labeled input-output example pair). The optimization however targets a SET of L demonstrations assembled across experts.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced: the training-set demonstration pool is partitioned offline via K-means clustering into C expert groups; per-expert retrievers are trained offline and frozen. No online/test-time growth.
index_structure_topology: Cluster-based / partitioned: the demonstration pool is split by K-means (Sentence-BERT embeddings) into C semantically-coherent clusters, each governed by one expert. Number of clusters C chosen adaptively via within-cluster SSE plus a lambda*C regularization term. Within each expert, retrieval is a flat dense-vector similarity search.
retriever_type: Learned dense retriever, one per expert (bi-encoder dual towers: g(x,e) = <M_d(e), M_q(x)>). A mixture of multiple learning-based dense retrievers; expert routing uses cosine similarity between query embedding and cluster centroid.
retriever_learning_signal: LM-feedback / downstream-task-effectiveness: per-expert scorers are trained with contrastive learning where positive/negative labels come from the LLM's few-shot output log-probability P_M(y | demo set, x) used as a utility proxy. Crucially scored in a FEW-SHOT pattern (candidate demo paired with the optimally-selected S_- of the other experts), inspired by coordinate descent, so the signal reflects set-level marginal contribution rather than singleton utility.
query_construction: Raw test input x_test is embedded (Sentence-BERT) to (a) route to experts via cosine similarity to cluster centroids h(C_i, x_test) and (b) score candidate demonstrations within each expert via the learned dual-encoder query tower. No query decomposition or expansion.
query_granularity: Task-level / per-test-example: a single retrieval is performed for each test query at inference (one-shot, t=0). No step-level or trajectory-level re-querying.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: the full L-sized demonstration set is retrieved once per test query before LLM inference.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval always occurs once per test query before prediction; no uncertainty/confidence/reflection-based triggering.
reranking: No explicit separate reranking stage. Selection is via per-expert top-scored demonstrations under quotas; during training a top-K candidate set is scored by the LLM and filtered (top-Ke positives), but this is a training-data construction step, not a test-time reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: Distractor filtering during training: the expert-wise (coordinate-descent-inspired) objective and few-shot scoring filter out unhelpful demonstrations so the learned scorers prefer set-compatible demonstrations. At inference, no post-retrieval refinement/compression beyond per-expert top-k selection under quotas.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools; demonstrations are raw labeled example pairs, not tool docstrings).
index_content_separation: N/A -- no separate lightweight-index-then-content scheme; clusters store full demonstrations.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (not a tool-retrieval setting). However, inter-DEMONSTRATION interaction IS modeled via set-level expert-wise training (analogous concept for demos).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the retrieved demonstration set S(x_test) is prepended as in-context examples to the frozen LLM, which predicts y_hat = argmax_y P_M(y | S(x_test), x_test). Retrieval is also used as a training signal during the offline scorer-training phase.
planning_integration: N/A for planning -- this is one-shot exemplar selection at prediction time (retrieve-then-predict). Not integrated with multi-step planning, tree search, or acting loops.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer: retrieval happens once and conditions a single LLM forward prediction; no per-step or per-token interleaving.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not CBR). Retrieved demonstrations are used verbatim as ICL exemplars; no case adaptation/revision.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw labeled demonstration example pairs (input-output) injected verbatim as few-shot exemplars in the prompt.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw single demonstration (concrete labeled example), assembled into a diverse set; no distilled strategy/guideline/workflow abstraction.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Expert-wise (coordinate-descent-inspired) training: when optimizing the score of a candidate demonstration, the other L-1 demonstrations are held fixed at their optimally-selected values, so unhelpful demonstrations do not corrupt the supervision signal; this directly targets the 'insufficient optimization / noise from unhelpful demonstrations' challenge. Clustering experts also reduces search space and noise.
memory_type: none (static demonstration pool; no episodic/skill/workflow memory written or evolved).
write_back: False -- the system does not store new experiences/cases during deployment; the demonstration pool and trained retrievers are fixed after offline training.
online_growth: False -- the retrievable store is frozen after offline K-means partitioning and per-expert scorer training; it does not grow at test time.
failure_experience_usage: No persistent storage of failures. During offline training, contrastive learning uses negatives including a hard demonstration (lowest few-shot score) and hard negatives from other batch samples, but these are training-time negatives, not a stored failure memory.
memory_evolution_update: N/A -- no memory store is mutated; retrievers are trained once offline (append-only training data per epoch into per-expert D_train, but no evolving deployed memory).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially: per-expert retrievers are LEARNED dense scorers trained via contrastive learning on LLM-feedback (not RL); expert assignment is fixed K-means + cosine-centroid routing. It is a learned-selection method rather than a fixed similarity-only top-k, but not an RL/value-based policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A / single-model: trained retrievers are shown to TRANSFER across LLMs (trained on GPT-Neo, applied to GPT2-XL, LLaMA-7B, GPT3.5), but this is model transferability, not shared multi-agent memory.
benchmarks: 12 NLP datasets. Classification: SST-5 (sentiment), MRPC (paraphrase), MNLI & QNLI (NLI), CMSQA/CommonsenseQA & HellaSwag (commonsense reasoning). Generation: WebQs (open-domain QA), GeoQuery & NL2Bash (code generation), Break, MTOP, SMCalFlow (semantic parsing). Compositional splits: GeoQuery (Standard/Template/TMCD/Length) and SMCalFlow-CS (S non-compositional / C cross-domain).
benchmark_family: QA (WebQs, CMSQA, HellaSwag) + classification/NLI (SST-5, MRPC, MNLI, QNLI) + code/semantic-parsing generation (GeoQuery, NL2Bash, Break, MTOP, SMCalFlow). Not in the agent/web/embodied/tool/memory families; this is an ICL demonstration-retrieval benchmark suite (following CEIL).
baselines: Learning-free: Random, TopK-BM25, TopK-Contriever (TopK-C), TopK-SimCSE (TopK-S), TopK-BERT. Learning-based: EPR (Rubin et al. 2022), CEIL (Ye et al. 2023, the prior SOTA). Ablations: MoD w/o E (no mixture-of-experts) and MoD w/o C (no expert-wise/coordinate-descent training).
key_metrics: Accuracy for classification tasks; Exact Match (EM) for generation tasks except Break which uses LF-EM (semantic-equivalence-aware EM). Reported as per-dataset scores plus a 12-dataset average and absolute gain (Delta) over CEIL.
headline_result: MoD reaches 58.63 average across the 12 datasets vs 56.76 for the prior SOTA CEIL, a +1.87 absolute average gain (GPT-Neo 2.7B). Largest single-task gain +6.06 on CMSQA (43.24 vs 37.18). On compositional GeoQuery-Standard, 77.38 vs 73.21 CEIL (+4.17).
ablations: Two key components ablated on SST-5, CMSQA, GeoQuery, MTOP: (1) MoD w/o E removes the mixture-of-experts design -> significant drop across all datasets, especially classification (SST-5, CMSQA), showing experts are critical for retrieving diverse/complex demonstrations; (2) MoD w/o C removes expert-wise (coordinate-descent-inspired) training -> moderate drop, showing its role in optimization. Additional studies: reduction of #ICL demonstrations (Fig.2) and cross-LLM transfer robustness (Table 4: retrievers trained on GPT-Neo / LLaMA-7B transferred to GPT2-XL, LLaMA-7B, GPT3.5).
evaluation_decoupling: No -- only end-to-end task metrics (accuracy / EM / LF-EM) are reported; no separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG). Selection quality is judged solely through downstream ICL task performance.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Outcome-only: final ICL prediction accuracy / EM. No intermediate process/faithfulness metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Argued qualitatively: partitioning the pool into experts reduces the retrieval search space (|D|^L is infeasible; experts cover the space without high cost, omitting experts whose quota floors to 0). MoD is shown to require less data (strong on small datasets like GeoQuery 404 train) and to maintain gains when the number of ICL demonstrations is reduced (Sec 4.4). No explicit latency/API-cost/token-savings numbers reported. [uncertain on concrete cost figures]
context_budget_and_selection_count: L (number of in-context demonstrations) set to 50, then truncated when combined length exceeds the LLM's max context per task; average #demos per task ranges ~22-50 (e.g., SMCalFlow 22, NL2Bash 43, SST-5/MNLI/CMSQA/HellaSwag/WebQs/GeoQuery 50). Per-expert counts are budget-allocated by quota |S_i| = floor(h(C_i, x_test) * L). Reduction-of-demonstrations study (Sec 4.4) varies the count.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a new benchmark; reuses CEIL/EPR datasets). Compositional splits (GeoQuery Template/TMCD/Length, SMCalFlow-CS S/C) are processed by CEIL [57] to require precise multi-demonstration retrieval.
builds_on: Mixture of Experts (Jacobs et al. 1991; Shazeer et al. 2017); coordinate descent (Wright); EPR (Rubin et al. 2022, contrastive demonstration scorer with LM feedback) and CEIL (Ye et al. 2023, set-level demonstration selection / DPP, the immediate SOTA predecessor extended here); Sentence-BERT (Reimers & Gurevych 2019) embeddings; learning-based ICL retrieval line including UDR (Li et al. 2023).
contrasts_with: Contrasts with singleton scorers EPR/UDR (ignore demonstration interactions) and with CEIL (which narrows candidates via a K-NN retriever before set selection, risking suboptimal sets due to insufficient exploration and exponential search space). Also contrasts with learning-free TopK methods (BM25, Contriever, SimCSE, BERT) that ignore LLM feedback. MoD instead partitions the whole pool into experts (covering dissimilar-but-useful demos) and uses expert-wise training to model set interaction without exhaustive search.
lineage: Group A (ICL demonstration retrieval). Sits in the learning-based demonstration-retrieval lineage EPR -> UDR -> CEIL -> MoD, advancing from singleton/DPP set selection to a mixture-of-experts partition with coordinate-descent-inspired set-aware training for large/noisy demonstration pools.
